records.title: Proportions
key_ideas: Unknown quantities can be found using proportional relationships.
relationships: Proportions build on ratios and support percentages and rates.
misconceptions: Assuming any two fractions form a proportion.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Percentages
records.definition: A way of expressing a quantity as a number of parts per hundred.
key_ideas: Percentages can represent proportions and changes.
relationships: Percentages are related to fractions, decimals, ratios and proportions.
misconceptions: Confusing percentage points with percentage change.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Factors
records.definition: Integers that divide another integer exactly without leaving a remainder.
key_ideas: Every positive integer has at least one and itself as positive factors.
principles: A factor multiplied by its paired factor produces the original number.
relationships: Factors are related to multiplication, divisibility and prime factorization.
assessment_ideas: Find all factors of given integers.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Multiples
records.definition: Numbers obtained by multiplying a given number by an integer.
key_ideas: Multiples form a sequence generated by multiplication.
A number is a multiple of another when it is their integer product.
principles: Every nonzero integer has infinitely many positive multiples.
relationships: Multiples are related to multiplication, factors and divisibility.
assessment_ideas: List multiples and identify common multiples.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions

records.title: Prime Numbers
records.definition: Positive integers greater than one that have exactly two positive divisors: one and themselves.
key_ideas: A prime number has exactly two positive divisors.
Two is the only even prime number.
principles: Every integer greater than one can be expressed uniquely as a product of primes, apart from order.
relationships: Prime numbers are related to factors, divisibility and number theory.
assessment_ideas: Identify primes and factor composite numbers.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard mathematical definitions
